c01-orders: GROUP BY produces one result per order and date. COUNT counts line identifiers; SUM totals their amounts. The inner SELECT defines the fixed order population. ORDER BY makes the result repeatable.
c01-fulfillment: WITH names two temporary results inside this statement: shipped and billed. Each is first summed by SalesOrderLineID. The final LEFT JOIN retains every selected order line, and COALESCE shows zero when no dated event exists. This avoids multiplying shipment and invoice detail against each other.
c01-invoices: This result has one invoice header per row. The order subquery selects the cohort, but invoice dates remain unrestricted so both reporting cutoffs can be reconstructed later.
c01-applications: Each result is one application. ReceiptAmount repeats when one receipt funds several applications. Sum AppliedAmount for invoice settlement; use distinct receipt IDs when describing received cash.
c01-balances: The cutoffs result contains the two review dates. CROSS JOIN pairs each date with each selected invoice, and the invoice-date condition excludes bills not yet issued. Each correlated SUM reads only applications or credits for that invoice through that date. Summarize the resulting rows separately by AsOf.
c01-ledger: Keep each SourceDocumentType/SourceDocumentID pair together. The same numeric ID can occur in unrelated source tables. Joining Account adds names without changing the posting grain.
c02-time: substr(WorkDate,1,7) creates a month key from the stored ISO date. GROUP BY engagement and month keeps different engagements separate. CASE includes billable hours only when approval occurred by the cutoff.
c02-billing: The correlated SUM uses the billing line’s engagement and inclusive coverage dates, plus approval by InvoiceDate. It returns one hours total per billing row without expanding that row once for every time entry.
c02-bridge: effort and billing each return one aggregate row before they are combined. The ratio uses all selected hours; the difference uses billed line amounts and recorded time cost with the stated boundary.
c03-matches: One result row is one matched supplier invoice line. The two correlated payment totals are calculated independently. InvoiceDate limits subsequent evidence to June 30; it does not imply payment by that date.
c03-goods-balances: events selects liability postings for the known receipt, invoice, and payment population. Credit minus debit gives a positive liability. Each cutoff sums only postings on or before its date. This measures posted GRNI rather than subtracting supplier price from standard receipt cost.
c03-accruals: LEFT JOIN retains an estimate even if its invoice link is missing. AccrualJournalEntryID supplies the relationship. The later invoice amount is displayed beside the original estimate rather than replacing it.
c04-comparison: Each group uses sums from the same invoice-line population. RealizationPct is a ratio of dollar totals, not an average of percentages. NULLIF leaves a zero-denominator ratio unavailable. CurrentStandardCost uses the current master reference explicitly.
c04-service: ShipmentLineID identifies the shipment supporting each billed line. The counts therefore describe invoice lines, not distinct customers or orders. A separate CASE retains the missing-delivery-date count.
c05-costs: Four named results summarize issues, labor, completions, and closes separately by WorkOrderID. LEFT JOIN adds these totals to the fixed release cohort. Missing close totals stay null, distinguishing an unclosed order from a zero variance.
c05-contrast: This repeats the same independently aggregated cost method for WO1 and WO67. It is executable by itself; it does not depend on a temporary table created in another step.
c05-capacity: Daily schedule totals are joined to the calendar before work-center aggregation. DaysAboveCapacity counts daily peaks; comparing only two period totals would lose them.
c06-coverage: Roster, load, and worked are separate work-center summaries. Their units and inclusion rules remain visible even though they share a center key. The center master retains centers with no activity.
c06-pay: hours groups by EmployeeID and PayrollPeriodID before joining payroll. A null hours result is retained for a register without approved hourly support. COUNT(DISTINCT WorkCenterID) records location variety without repeating pay across locations.
c06-unpaid: LEFT JOIN keeps the payroll registers; a null PayrollPaymentID identifies unmatched payment evidence. This is a test of records in the release, not proof of what happened outside it.
c07-rollforward: The WHERE clause has only an upper date boundary. CASE separates all earlier history from quarter activity. All amounts use debit minus credit, so opening plus movement equals closing on one consistent sign basis.
c07-profit: The journal join applies only when the source type is JournalEntry. COALESCE preserves operational entries with no journal match, while NOT LIKE excludes the annual close. Profit uses credit minus debit for revenue and expense accounts.
c07-bridge: Exclude cash and revenue/expense accounts, keep quarter activity, and remove annual close entries. Credit minus debit on the remaining accounts supplies the effects needed to bridge pre-close profit to cash. HAVING removes immaterial zero aggregates after grouping.
c08-duplicates: groups identifies exact supplier/reference pairs occurring more than once. Joining the group back retrieves each flagged document. The payment SUM is independent, so multiple payments cannot duplicate invoice values.
c08-checks: Blank references are excluded before grouping. The same supplier and CheckNumber must match. Keep both group counts and payment-row counts; they answer different questions.
c08-overtime: LEFT JOIN retains missing approvals. CASE applies the hours-support criteria in order: no linked record, insufficient approved hours, then hours supported. The WHERE clause fixes the eligible quarter, approved clock status, and positive overtime denominator.
